Next item by maximum Fisher information

Source: R/fct_rsm.R
next_item_rsm.Rd

Picks, among the items not yet given, the one with the most information at the current ability estimate. Under the rating scale model this is the item whose \(\lambda_j\) is nearest to \(\theta\). With randomesque = 1 it returns the same item as catR::nextItem(model = "RSM", criterion = "MFI").

Usage

next_item_rsm(theta, bank, out = NULL, D = 1, randomesque = 1)

Arguments

theta

Current ability estimate.

bank

Matrix of item parameters, one row per item: column 1 is the location of the item \(\lambda_j\), the other columns the thresholds \(\delta_1\) to \(\delta_m\), the same in every row (which makes it the rating scale and not the partial credit model). A 5-point Likert item, scored 0 to 4, needs 5 columns.

out

Indices of the items already given.

D

Metric constant, 1 or 1.702.

randomesque

Number of most informative items to draw one from at random: 1 is pure maximum information, 3 to 5 spreads the exposure of the items.

Value

A list: item, the index of the selected item in the bank, info, its information at theta, and available, the indices of the items that were still available.

See also

Other rating scale model: Ii_rsm(), Pi_rsm(), density_function(), eap_est_rsm(), eap_se_rsm(), integrate_cat(), likelihood_rsm()

Examples

bank <- matrix(c(-0.560, -0.230, 1.559, 0.071, 0.129,
                 rep(1.715, 5), rep(0.461, 5), rep(-1.265, 5), rep(-0.687, 5)),
               nrow = 5,
               dimnames = list(1:5, c("lambdaj", "delta1", "delta2", "delta3", "delta4")))
next_item_rsm(theta = 0, bank)
#> $item
#> [1] 4
#> 
#> $info
#> [1] 3.061434
#> 
#> $available
#> [1] 1 2 3 4 5
#> 
next_item_rsm(theta = 1.5, bank, out = c(4, 5))
#> $item
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $info
#> [1] 3.076108
#> 
#> $available
#> [1] 1 2 3
#> 
# a short adaptive test
responses <- c()
administered <- c()
theta <- 0
for (step in 1:4) {
  item <- next_item_rsm(theta, bank, out = administered)$item
  administered <- c(administered, item)
  responses <- c(responses, 4) # the answer, scored 0 to 4
  theta <- eap_est_rsm(bank[administered, , drop = FALSE], responses)
  cat("step", step, "item", item, "theta", round(theta, 4),
      "se", round(eap_se_rsm(theta, bank[administered, , drop = FALSE], responses), 4), "\n")
}
#> step 1 item 4 theta 0.8477 se 0.6921 
#> step 2 item 5 theta 1.0943 se 0.6324 
#> step 3 item 3 theta 1.8299 se 0.5575 
#> step 4 item 2 theta 1.8537 se 0.553
